title: Collatz Conjecture: Reduction to Odd Inputs
description: Proves, axiom-free, the structural reduction of the Collatz conjecture to odd numbers: every n ≥ 1 reaches 1 iff every odd n ≥ 1 does. Built on one-step invariance of the reaching set (ReachesOne (collatz n) ↔ ReachesOne n) and doubling invariance (ReachesOne (2^m·n) ↔ ReachesOne n). Strengthened to the accelerated Syracuse map n ↦ (3n+1)/2^v₂(3n+1): for odd n the Syracuse and Collatz reaching predicates coincide (reachesOne_iff_syrReachesOne), so the conjecture is equivalent to its Syracuse form (collatz_iff_syracuse). The conjecture itself remains open; this organizes the search space.

meta.assumptions: None. 0 axioms, 0 sorries. The file imports Proofs.CollatzStructured (which declares the conjecture as an axiom) but no theorem here uses that axiom — every result is proved from the sInf-free dynamical definitions and Mathlib's 2-adic factorization API (ordCompl/ordProj). #print axioms collatz_reduces_to_odd and #print axioms collatz_iff_syracuse both report only propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound (no sorryAx, no custom axiom). The Collatz conjecture itself is NOT proved; the reduction is an equivalence between two open statements.

overview.historicalContext: The Collatz conjecture (1937, Lothar Collatz) asks whether iterating n ↦ n/2 (n even), n ↦ 3n+1 (n odd) always reaches 1. It is unsolved. A standard first observation in the literature is that the problem only needs to be settled for odd inputs: an even number simply halves until an odd number is reached, so its fate is determined by that odd number. This entry formalizes that reduction rigorously in Lean 4. The gallery's other Collatz entries cover powers of two (parent collatz-structured), cycle exclusion (collatz-cycles family), and stopping-time asymptotics (collatz-structured-oq-03); the odd reduction — equivalence of the conjecture with its odd restriction — was not previously formalized.
overview.problemStatement: Let ReachesOne(n) mean some Collatz iterate of n equals 1. Show that (∀ n ≥ 1, ReachesOne n) is equivalent to (∀ odd m ≥ 1, ReachesOne m), so the Collatz conjecture reduces to the odd case. The conjecture itself is left open.
overview.proofStrategy: The reaching set S = {n | ReachesOne n} is invariant under one step of the dynamics in both directions: forward (drop the first iterate, with the n=1 base case using collatz 1 = 4 = 2²) and backward (prepend a step). This gives reachesOne_collatz_iff. Specializing to even inputs, collatz(2n) = n yields ReachesOne (2n) ↔ ReachesOne n, and induction lifts this to ReachesOne (2^m · n) ↔ ReachesOne n. Finally, writing n = 2^v₂(n) · oddPart n via Mathlib's ordProj/ordCompl factorization, with oddPart n odd and positive, the equivalence ReachesOne n ↔ ReachesOne (oddPart n) follows, and the headline reduction collatz_reduces_to_odd is immediate.
prerequisites: 2-adic valuation and the factorization n = 2^v₂(n) · (odd part)
keyInsights: The reaching set is invariant under the Collatz map in BOTH directions: ReachesOne (collatz n) ↔ ReachesOne n. Backward is a free prepend; forward needs only the n=1 base case, where collatz 1 = 4 = 2² reaches 1 by the powers-of-two lemma.

Doubling invariance is an equivalence, not just closure: the parent file proved ReachesOne n → ReachesOne (2n); the reverse follows from forward one-step invariance plus collatz(2n) = n, completing ReachesOne (2n) ↔ ReachesOne n.
Stripping all factors of two preserves reachability: ReachesOne (2^m · n) ↔ ReachesOne n by induction on m. Hence n and its odd part oddPart n = ordCompl[2] n are equireachable.

The reduction is exact: the full conjecture is logically equivalent to its restriction to odd inputs, so a minimal counterexample (if any) may be taken odd. This halves the search space conceptually but does not bring the open problem closer to resolution.

The file is genuinely axiom-free: it imports the parent (which axiomatizes the conjecture) but no theorem here uses that axiom — a contrast with the axiom-bearing sibling entries (Terras density, Eliahou bound).

sections.title: One-step invariance of the reaching set
sections.summary: ReachesOne (collatz n) ↔ ReachesOne n, via backward (prepend) and forward (drop, n=1 base case) directions
sections.mathContext: The set of numbers reaching 1 is invariant under the Collatz map in both directions. The forward base case n=1 uses collatz 1 = 4 = 2².

sections.title: Doubling and power-of-two invariance
sections.summary: ReachesOne (2·n) ↔ ReachesOne n and ReachesOne (2^m·n) ↔ ReachesOne n
sections.mathContext: collatz(2n) = n composed with one-step invariance gives the reverse of the parent's doubling closure; induction lifts to arbitrary powers of two.

sections.title: The odd part and equireachability
sections.summary: oddPart n = ordCompl[2] n is odd and positive; n = 2^v₂(n)·oddPart n; ReachesOne (oddPart n) ↔ ReachesOne n
sections.mathContext: Mathlib's 2-adic factorization splits n into its 2-power part and odd part; reachability is invariant under removing the 2-power part.

sections.title: Reduction to the odd case
sections.mathContext: The conjecture for all n ≥ 1 is equivalent to the conjecture for odd n ≥ 1; counterexamples may be taken odd.

sections.title: The Syracuse (accelerated odd) map and full equivalence
sections.summary: syracuse n = oddPart (3n+1); collatz_iter_eq_syracuse realises it in v₂(3n+1)+1 steps; reachesOne_iff_syrReachesOne and collatz_iff_syracuse
sections.mathContext: The accelerated odd map does the 3n+1 step and strips all resulting powers of two at once. It is realised by finitely many ordinary Collatz steps, and for odd inputs its reaching predicate coincides exactly with the Collatz one (per-step, iterated, and full equivalence). Hence the Collatz conjecture is equivalent to its Syracuse form. The converse direction (Collatz-reaching ⟹ Syracuse-reaching) is proved by strong induction on the Collatz step count, using that the trajectory of an odd n > 1 cannot reach 1 before the accelerated step.

conclusion.summary: With zero axioms, this entry reduces the Collatz conjecture to its restriction to odd inputs: (∀ n ≥ 1, ReachesOne n) ↔ (∀ odd m ≥ 1, ReachesOne m). The machinery is the two-directional invariance of the reaching set under the Collatz map and under multiplication by powers of two. The conjecture itself remains open.
conclusion.implications: The reduction is the standard first simplification of the Collatz problem and is now formalized. It shows the reaching set is a dynamically invariant set closed under the 2-adic structure, so any attack on Collatz may restrict to odd numbers without loss. The one-step and doubling equivalences are reusable building blocks for further structural work (e.g. the Syracuse/accelerated map on odd numbers). None of this lowers the difficulty of the open conjecture; it organizes the state space.
openQuestions: The Collatz conjecture itself: does every odd n ≥ 1 reach 1?
Can the reduction be pushed further (e.g. to n ≡ 3 mod 4, or to the Syracuse map) with a comparably clean Lean formalization?
Is there a Lean-formalizable invariant that distinguishes odd numbers by residue class and interacts well with this reduction?

mainTheorems.name: reachesOne_collatz_iff
mainTheorems.description: One-step invariance: n reaches 1 iff its Collatz successor does

mainTheorems.name: reachesOne_pow_two_mul_iff
mainTheorems.description: Power-of-two invariance: 2^m·n reaches 1 iff n does
mainTheorems.leanType: ∀ m n, ReachesOne (2 ^ m * n) ↔ ReachesOne n

mainTheorems.name: collatz_reduces_to_odd
mainTheorems.description: The Collatz conjecture reduces to odd inputs: all n ≥ 1 reach 1 iff all odd n ≥ 1 do
mainTheorems.leanType: (∀ n, n ≥ 1 → ReachesOne n) ↔ (∀ m, m ≥ 1 → m % 2 = 1 → ReachesOne m)

mainTheorems.name: collatz_counterexample_odd
mainTheorems.description: Any Collatz counterexample implies an odd counterexample
mainTheorems.leanType: (∃ n, n ≥ 1 ∧ ¬ ReachesOne n) → ∃ m, m ≥ 1 ∧ m % 2 = 1 ∧ ¬ ReachesOne m

mainTheorems.name: reachesOne_iff_syrReachesOne
mainTheorems.description: For odd n, the Syracuse and Collatz reaching predicates coincide

mainTheorems.name: collatz_iff_syracuse
mainTheorems.description: The Collatz conjecture is equivalent to its accelerated Syracuse form: every n ≥ 1 reaches 1 iff every odd m ≥ 1 reaches 1 under n ↦ (3n+1)/2^v₂(3n+1)
mainTheorems.leanType: (∀ n, n ≥ 1 → ReachesOne n) ↔ (∀ m, m ≥ 1 → m % 2 = 1 → SyrReachesOne m)

crossReferences.description: The parent file defines the Collatz map, ReachesOne, the powers-of-two lemma, and doubling closure; this entry strengthens doubling closure to an equivalence and derives the odd reduction.
Both study structural reductions of the Collatz problem; the stopping-time entry uses the 2-adic valuation for asymptotics, this entry uses it (via ordCompl) for the odd reduction.
Cycle-exclusion results constrain periodic orbits; the odd reduction constrains where a counterexample could live (odd numbers), a complementary structural narrowing.
